subject: design-studies
title: Ergonomic Dimensions: Fit the Chair and Desk to the Student Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says one standard size fits every user, because a chair built to average measurements fits each person who sits in it. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - an average size is close enough for every body

Ergonomic design sizes the product from the user own measurements: seat height from the lower-leg height, seat width from the hip breadth plus clearance, and desk height from the seat height plus the seated elbow height.
The chair should be sized for the smallest student only
Fit does not matter as long as the chair is strong enough

questions.misconception: One standard size fits every user, because a chair built to average measurements fits each person who sits in it.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: One standard size fits every user, because a chair built to average measurements fits each person who sits in it. Reteach point: Ergonomic design sizes the product from the user's own measurements: the seat height is set to the lower-leg height so the feet rest flat, the seat width to the hip breadth plus clearance, and the desk height to the seat height plus the seated elbow height - a chair built to the average leaves every gap open for anyone who is not average.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, give the desk height for a student whose seat height is 40 cm and whose seated elbow height is 24 cm, and say how it is set.
questions.answer: The desk height is 64 cm, set as the seat height plus the seated elbow height (40 + 24) so the forearms rest level.
questions.feedback: A strong answer shows the build-up: desk height comes from the seat plus the elbow height, not from a standard table.

questions.prompt: In the animation, the feet rest flat on the floor when:

choices.text: The seat is at the standard average height
The seat height has risen to equal the lower-leg height
The desk height matches the seat width

questions.feedback: Scene 2 shows the gap under the thigh closing exactly when the seat height reaches the lower-leg height of 40 cm.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, name the three measurements taken from the student and what each one sets.
questions.answer: The lower-leg height sets the seat height, the hip breadth plus clearance sets the seat width, and the seated elbow height (added to the seat height) sets the desk height.
questions.feedback: A strong answer pairs every dimension with its measurement - no dimension comes from an average.
